title: Smoked Carnitas
summary: Pork shoulder cut into chunks, smoked for bark, braised in citrus and chipotle, then crisped in cast iron.

ingredients.prep: cut into 2 1/2-inch chunks, thick fat cap trimmed

steps.title: Rub
steps.text: Mix the rub and coat every chunk of pork.

steps.title: Dry-brine
steps.text: Let it sit while the grill heats, about an hour.

steps.title: Smoke
steps.text: Smoke at 250°F with hickory, oak, or a fruitwood blend, chunks spaced apart on the grates, until 160 to 170°F inside with a deep mahogany bark that doesn't smear when touched, 2 to 2 1/2 hours. If it's colored but under temp, move on; if it's at temp but pale, leave it.

steps.title: Mix the braise
steps.text: Stir the orange juice, lime juice, broth, chipotles, and adobo. Use room-temperature liquid if braising in stoneware.

steps.title: Load the pans
steps.text: Pack the chunks snugly into two pans (a 13x9 holds about 5 to 6 lb). Tuck in the onion, garlic, bay leaves, orange halves, and cinnamon stick. Pour in the liquid to about a third of the way up the meat, scatter the lard on top, and crimp foil on tight.

steps.title: Braise
steps.text: Raise the grill to 300°F and braise until a fork twists through a chunk with no resistance, around 200 to 205°F, 1 1/2 to 2 hours. Give it more time rather than serving it tough.

steps.title: Strain the juices
steps.text: Lift out the pork. Pour the juices into a fat separator, mash the soft garlic into them, and discard the orange halves, bay, and cinnamon. Simmer the juices 5 to 10 minutes if they taste thin.

steps.title: Crisp
steps.text: Break the pork into rough pieces and crisp in batches in a hot cast-iron pan with spoonfuls of the skimmed fat. Don't crowd the pan. Spoon juices over just before serving with warm tortillas.

notes: Cutting the shoulder into chunks triples the bark and gets you whole-shoulder texture in about half the time, skipping the stall. Stoneware: room-temperature liquid going in, and set it on a dry towel or trivet coming out.
